content:
Marissa Cole: Want to sanity check PRD scope before we lock Phase 1 tickets. Biggest open Q: do we report by “route” (path + method) vs “endpoint group” (normalized route + product label)?

Paula Mendes: +1. Also need alignment on beta criteria + export expectations (finance keeps asking for CSV that matches invoice totals).

Dylan Brooks: From console POV: users will think in “endpoint” not “route”. But our data will be keyed off gateway route. If we expose raw route strings, it’ll get messy (dynamic IDs etc).

Chloe Martin: Agree. Backend can do both but we need one canonical dimension to aggregate on or we’ll blow up cardinality.

Logan Wright: Telemetry today has `http.path` and `api_route` (inconsistent). For analytics we should define a single `route_canonical` + `route_display`. Canonical is templated, display is friendly.

Nadia Rahman: +1 on canonicalization. Billing attribution also needs a stable key. If we keep switching naming, reconciliation will be a nightmare.

Marissa Cole: So proposal: UI label = “Endpoint” but underlying dimension = normalized “route”. In docs/tooltips we explain endpoint == normalized route. Does that work?

Alex Martinez: That’s basically what we discussed in DevEx review. “Route” reads too infrastructure-y. Suggest: UI says “Endpoint”, filters say “Endpoint (normalized)”, tooltip: “We group dynamic paths (e.g. /v1/projects/123 → /v1/projects/:id).”

Dylan Brooks: Works for me. UX needs an escape hatch though: if route normalization fails, we should bucket into “Unnormalized / Other” not show 10k unique paths.

Chloe Martin: Yep. Guardrail in query service: if `route_canonical` missing, map to `unknown_route` and show a banner “Some requests are missing endpoint tags” + link to docs.

Logan Wright: Important: OpenAI-compat endpoints (/v1/chat/completions etc) also exist behind a few proxy prefixes. Normalization library must strip the prefix consistently. Otherwise we’ll get duplicates.

Paula Mendes: Can we document the normalization rules in an ADR and link from PRD? I want that locked before ENG starts aggregation.

Marissa Cole: Yes, let’s do ADR. Dylan/Chloe can you own? Logan can review.

Dylan Brooks: 👍 will draft. We’ll include: method+path, templating rules, prefix stripping, and fallback/retry attribution.

Nadia Rahman: On retries/fallbacks: we need to decide whether cost is attributed to the *final* model/route or includes failed attempts. Finance wants “total spend”, engineering wants “waste”.

Marissa Cole: My read: Phase 1 shows totals aligned to billing (includes retries/fallbacks), but we add separate columns for “retries cost” and “fallback cost” as drivers.

Paula Mendes: That matches the goals section. Also helps “what changed?” explainers (“retries increased”).

Chloe Martin: Implementation detail: events are per attempt. We can aggregate: `attempt_count`, `successful_request_count`, `retry_token_in/out`, `fallback_model` etc. But UI needs to be careful not to double count.

Dylan Brooks: +1. In table we should have a single “Total cost” column (matches billing) + expandable “drivers” (tokens in/out, cache miss, retries, streaming overhead). Otherwise it becomes a spreadsheet.

Alex Martinez: Re terminology: “cache hit/miss” is confusing if users don’t know if it’s prefix/KV cache vs HTTP cache. Tooltip should say “Prompt prefix cache (server-side).”

Elliot Price: Noted. Docs can have a “Definitions” section + common pitfalls (streaming adds overhead, retries count, fallbacks show up under original endpoint).

Markus Klein: From SE perspective: beta customers will ask “does this match my invoice?” immediately. We should set expectations: there’s lag + rounding differences, and maybe exclusions (credits/taxes).

Paula Mendes: Let’s define beta success criteria explicitly. What’s acceptable drift vs billing?

Nadia Rahman: For beta I’d target: daily totals within 1% OR $5 (whichever higher), excluding credits/discounts, and we surface the reconciliation timestamp.

Logan Wright: Data freshness: warehouse lag can be up to ~90m during peak. If we promise “near real time” we’ll get paged. Suggest SLO: 95% of time buckets complete within 2 hours; UI shows “last updated”.

Dylan Brooks: Console can show a “Data may be delayed by up to 2 hours” info label + a warning banner when lag > 4h.

Marissa Cole: Great. Beta criteria draft:
1) Route+model breakdown available for allowlisted accounts
2) Totals reconcile with billing within tolerance (1% or $5) for selected time ranges
3) Freshness p95 < 2h, banner if lagging
4) Export CSV available with same totals as table
5) RBAC: only Admin/Billing roles can view cost + export

Paula Mendes: Add performance target? We got feedback that analytics pages timing out is a non-starter.

Chloe Martin: For interactive queries: p95 < 2.5s for 7-day range, < 5s for 30-day range (with caching). If it’s slower, we should require users to narrow range.

Dylan Brooks: UI can enforce max range for beta (e.g., 30 days) and prompt to export for larger. That also helps load.

Markus Klein: Export expectations: Finance wants CSV with stable columns + currency + rounding rules. Also wants a file name they can automate around.

Elliot Price: Do we want export to be synchronous or async job?

Chloe Martin: Async only. Some customers will export 30 days x many endpoints/models; synchronous will time out and tie up workers. We should do: create export job → poll → signed URL.

Paula Mendes: Agree. In PRD we’ll set expectation: export may take a few minutes, link expires.

Nadia Rahman: And audit logging is required (who exported, filters, time range). Security will block without it.

Dylan Brooks: Export file naming: `usage-insights_{workspace}_{start}_{end}_{tz}.csv` (or similar). We can include a header comment row for filters, but some BI tools choke on that.

Markus Klein: Better: keep CSV pure (no comment rows). Put metadata in the export job details endpoint, not inside CSV.

Alex Martinez: +1. Also ensure column names are readable: `endpoint`, `model`, `token_in`, `token_out`, `cache_hit_rate`, `retries`, `total_cost_usd`. Don’t leak internal field names.

Marissa Cole: Action items:
- Paula: update PRD wording to “Endpoint (normalized route)” + add beta criteria + perf targets
- Dylan/Chloe: draft ADR for route normalization + share in this thread
- Logan/Nadia: confirm reconciliation tolerance + what’s excluded (credits/discounts)
- Markus/Alex/Elliot: review export column naming + docs/tooltips

Paula Mendes: Works. I’ll push PRD edits today and tag you all.

Dylan Brooks: I’ll post ADR draft tomorrow morning.

Logan Wright: I’ll drop a note on telemetry gaps too (missing route tags in streaming in one region) so we don’t surprise ourselves.

Marissa Cole: Perfect. Thanks all.
(reaction :thumbsup: from Paula Mendes)
(reaction :+1: from Chloe Martin)
(reaction :white_check_mark: from Markus Klein)
